clue.text: Sign writing

parts.note: read literally, writing done in signs or pictorial symbols, as on the walls of ancient Egyptian tombs, rather than painting shop signs

explanation.surface: A signwriter's trade, lettering shop fronts and pub boards.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests the craft of painting shop signs; read instead as writing made of signs, it describes the picture script of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian picture-script is literally writing composed of signs and symbols rather than letters.

clue.text: Guarantee compensation

definitions.meaning: a guarantee or security against loss or damage
money paid to make good a loss

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a promise of protection against loss and the payment made for that loss.

clue.text: Repeat soldiers' retreat

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to run away is to retreat

explanation.surface: An army retreat happens all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat showing of a programme is a second broadcast of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Shone like a newly minted medal, for example?

indicators.note: a newly minted object has been freshly cast, so the letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: A brand new medal glinting in the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly minted' recasts MEDAL and EG together; 'like a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaming is giving off bright reflected light, a synonym for shining.

clue.text: Unusually frosty around the north for 10

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the abbreviation for north
unusually means the letters of frosty are put in an unusual order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Frosty northern weather calls for something warm underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges FROSTY to YFROTS, and 'around' puts that round N. '10' points to the answer of 10-across, UNDERWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's briefs with a Y-shaped front seam are an example of underwear, the answer at 10.

clue.text: Upholstery material that is harsh or rough

indicators.note: rough means the letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: IE, abbreviation of id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Some stuffing for furniture is described as harsh or rough to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' reworks IE, HARSH and OR together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse hair from manes and tails was long used as stuffing for chairs and sofas, an upholstery material.

clue.text: Such plants have their points

parts.note: plants with spines literally have points, while the idiom says they have merits

explanation.surface: Certain plants have their good qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents are covered in spines, literally points, so they are the plants meant.

clue.text: Ruth upset after ruining the joyful holiday abroad

indicators.note: after places the reworked Ruth behind the other piece
ruining means the letters of the joyful are broken up and rebuilt
upset means the letters of Ruth are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Ruth is upset after something spoils a happy holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The holiday is American Independence Day, 'abroad' because the setter is British; the two anagrams sit in answer order, 'after' putting Ruth's letters last.
explanation.definitionFit: American Independence Day is a public holiday abroad from a British point of view.

clue.text: The girl's mother takes unusually hot pride in being bisexual

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of hot pride are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A girl's mother is unusually proud of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' only links; 'bisexual' is used in its biological sense of having both sexes' organs.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism with both male and female sex organs is described as bisexual in the biological sense.

clue.text: Possibly slips beneath surface of the river

parts.note: beneath means under
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: Someone slips below the surface of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks slips as one example; 'surface of' only links. The Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips, petticoats worn under a dress, are one example of clothing worn under other clothes.

clue.text: A fringe gathering of lace makers

definitions.text: A fringe gathering of lace makers

parts.words: A fringe gathering of lace makers
parts.note: sounds like a meeting of lacemakers on the fringes, but describes a gathered frill of lace itself

explanation.surface: A fringe meeting at a conference of lacemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of gathered or pleated fabric or lace used as trimming is exactly a frill made by gathering.

clue.text: The old soldiers of a country

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: The veteran soldiers of some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The republic in the south of the Arabian peninsula is a country.

clue.text: A peculiarity of men in arms

definitions.text: A peculiarity of men in arms

indicators.note: a peculiar version of the words that follow signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers have their own characteristic quirks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and 'A peculiarity of' also tells you to rearrange MEN IN ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual gesture or way of speaking is a personal peculiarity or quirk.

clue.text: In difficulty, so Edith given a lift

indicators.note: letters in difficulty are in trouble and disturbed, so so and Edith are rearranged

explanation.surface: Edith, having got into trouble, is offered a ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In difficulty' reworks SO EDITH into the answer; 'given a lift' means raised, not driven somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised up with ropes or tackle is a synonym for being lifted.

clue.text: Is it all leaves and no flowers?

definitions.text: Is it all leaves and no flowers?

parts.words: Is it all leaves and no flowers?
parts.note: a plot planted with nothing but leaves sounds odd, but a tea plantation is grown purely for its leaves; also a cafe garden where tea leaves are served

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a garden has only foliage and no blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation of tea bushes is cultivated only for its leaves, not its blossoms.

clue.text: Get fish in to eat for a complete change

indicators.note: in means the fish is placed inside the word for eating

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper
the hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Fetch some fish in for supper to make a nice change.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical reorganisation is a complete change of an organisation or system.

clue.text: Playbill

parts.note: split it in two: a performance of a play, and a bill passed into law

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the acting out of a play and a law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Run quickly over ceremony

parts.note: to fly is to move very fast
past means over, as in the time is over

explanation.surface: Hurry through a formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial flight of aircraft over a crowd is a display of ceremony.

clue.text: Exploded near the capital

indicators.note: exploded means the letters of near the are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Something blew up close to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploded' reworks NEAR THE into the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Iran, here in an older spelling.

clue.text: We hear vulgar shanty from this pirate

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a vulgar song is a coarse air

explanation.surface: A pirate is overheard singing a rude sea song.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE AIR, said out loud, gives the pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer of the Barbary coast was a pirate.

clue.text: A willing rider

parts.note: sounds like an eager horseman, but means a rider (addition) to a will

explanation.surface: A horseman who is happy to get in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement added to a will is a rider attached to that legal document.

clue.text: A bilingual graduate, put off but not disconcerted

parts.note: the word a given in two languages: un in French followed by a in English
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
to shed is to put off, as clothes

explanation.surface: A graduate fluent in two languages is put off but keeps composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual' asks for 'A' in two languages, French UN then English A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unembarrassed and composed is a synonym for not being disconcerted.

clue.text: Valediction announcement that is given to university

parts.note: an ad is an announcement
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A farewell speech is delivered at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is a word of valediction, or goodbye.

clue.text: Stuffed with chopped dates

indicators.note: chopped means the letters of dates are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Filled up on a dish of chopped dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full after eating plenty is a synonym for being stuffed.

clue.text: Has the neck to ask for credit during slump

indicators.note: during means credit comes in the middle of slump

parts.note: to sag is to slump

explanation.surface: Someone has the cheek to ask for a loan during a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has the neck' looks like cheek, but neck is the definition: the scrag is the bony neck of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrag end is the neck of a sheep, as a cut of meat.

clue.text: Time to organise raid to expose criminal gang

indicators.note: to organise means the letters of raid are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Police plan a raid to unmask a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expose' only links; the triads are Chinese criminal secret societies.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese secret criminal society is a gang of this name.

clue.text: Sappers meet general coming back

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are known as sappers
current means general or widespread, as in current belief

explanation.surface: Engineers meet their returning commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' reads as an army officer but means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps coming back again is recurring, a synonym.

clue.text: Put on at night by sailors smuggling cat food

definitions.text: Put on at night by sailors

parts.note: running guns or drink is smuggling them
lights are animal lungs, traditionally sold as cat food

explanation.surface: Sailors are caught smuggling pet food at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights are the lungs of slaughtered animals, once a staple British cat food.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigation lamps shown by a ship after dark are switched on by sailors at night.
